newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens ready to test share dematerialisation.
newsitem.headline: Athens ready to test share dematerialisation.

text.p: Back from a U.S. roadshow in New York and Boston, Athens stock exchange president Manolis Xanthakis said on Thursday the bourse was ready to launch a pilot programme on dematerialised shares next Monday.
"The bourse is launching its pilot programme on dematerialised shares on Monday. The software will be tested with five stocks to get rid of any possible bugs," Xanthakis told reporters.
The next step will be a timetable which will specify the phases of share dematerialisation -- the gradual conversion of paper securities to electronic book entry form.
This will begin with shares of some 100 listings which have been fully demobilised -- substituted with central depository share certificates.
"The objective is to complete share dematerialisation by the end of 1997," he said.

Xanthakis said a draft bill to introduce equity derivatives on the Athens stock exchange was ready and waiting for the initiative of the national economy ministry to be presented to parliament and become law.

Following up on his recent statements that short-selling would be permitted on the exchange before Christmas, he said the bourse's board of directors had approved the plan but it presupposed a regulatory framework for margin trading as well.
"Hopefully the required procedures for implementation on the part of the government will be fast. Procedures do take time," he said.

Responding to questions, Xanthakis acknowledged that the state's television ads to support sales of treasury paper were not helping attract funds to the equities market and this had been brought to the attention of Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis.
In its effort to promote the idea of equity investing domestically, the bourse is planning to disseminate promotional material countrywide.
Informational brochures will be enclosed in OTE telecom telephone bills and Diners Club statements. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
